evals.prompt: I'm running a master's study on how people accept an AI that cuts their home cooling during a heatwave. I need four interactive HTML prototypes for a 2x2 of agency (high/low) and community (shared building vs private). The outcome has to be unfavourable in all four, and I'll measure acceptance, fairness, and trust after each. Build them.
evals.expected_output: An intake (preferred-temperature) screen plus four cells C1-C4 that import one shared design system; matched pairs differ only on the intended axis; the unfavourable outcome is personalised and crosses a comfort threshold; procedural-fairness affordances (voice/appeal/what-ARKI-used) present in high-agency cells and absent in low; a measurement map and a manipulation-check summary.

evals.prompt: My cooling prototypes have way too much text, the four versions look inconsistent, and I can't tell what the main thing the user is supposed to do is. Can you fix them so they actually work as study stimuli?
evals.expected_output: Rebuilt cells on the shared design system: one visually dominant core action per screen (data-role=primary), body text under budget with context moved behind details affordances, identical layout/styling across cells with only the manipulated axis regions differing. check_prototype.py and matched_pairs_diff.py pass.

evals.prompt: Same cooling study, but I want to swap the agency axis for a transparency axis (the AI explains its reasoning a lot vs barely at all), keeping the community axis. Regenerate the four prototypes and tell me what changes in what I can measure.
evals.expected_output: A re-derived flow and measurement map for transparency x community; four matched cells where only transparency varies between C1/C3 and C2/C4; an updated item->hook table reflecting that procedural-fairness/voice hooks are replaced by explanation-depth hooks; matched-2x2 discipline preserved.
